messages:
olivia: Heads-up — ACME Apex asking for a combined API + Optimize + Console add-on package. They asked for ~30% off list if they commit 12 months and $1.2M. Any quick thoughts on how tight we are on that?

samir: 30% is high. Do we have their ARR/usage forecast? also is this blended or pure committed spend?

olivia: Forecast they shared: ~850k in year one, hitting 1.2M if new feature ships in Q3. It's a blended ask across API tokens + optimize compute + console seats. 

elena: For packaging i'd propose a tiered approach: 18% at $750k commit, 22% at $1M, 25% at $1.2M + credits for Console add-ons. POC terms: 60-day limited POC, non-prod SLA only. Also security asked for private VPC for prod POC — that's an add-on.

mike: can you paste the list SKUs and monthly equivalents so i can run the rate-card math? i'll need the SKU lines for deal desk justification.

olivia: sure — SKUs:
```
API-Tokens-STD: $0.0008/token
Optimize-Compute-Hour: $6/hr
Console-Seat: $600/seat/mo
Private-VPC: $10,000/mo
```

deal-desk-bot: Deal 1848604321 submitted to Deal Desk for pricing review (status: pending).

samir: Q: do we price Optimize as usage-based or can we offer an avg-usage cap for predictable billing? customer wants predictability.

elena: Recommend keeping Optimize usage-based but offer a committed bucket with discounted overage. Example: commit 10k compute hours @ 20% off, overage billed at list. Console should be flat add-on (one-time seat fee or annual).

olivia: i'll draft a term sheet: tiered discount + committed compute bucket + private VPC surcharge + 60-day POC clause. also include a canary fallback policy for model variants. @mike please kick off approval.

mike: starting routing now — will attach ROI and list-vs-proposed comparison. Also pls confirm whether quantization support / accelerated kernels are included in the price.

rebecca: legal note: need customer's SOC2 attestation and data retention policy before finalizing private deployment terms. also will request standard IP/data-use redlines.

olivia: thanks — i'll request SOC2 and retention doc from ACME. adding term sheet link when ready: https://redwood.example/term/ACME-1848604321 :thumbsup:

samir: one more: if finance needs a concession, can we trade on TCV/commit length rather than raw %? might be easier to accept.

elena: agreed — prefer to structure as multi-year commit (2yr) with step-down pricing instead of a one-off 30% deep discount. keeps unit economics intact.

olivia: perfect. i'll iterate and ping when i have the draft.
